scope: semantic requirements, not a proposed wire schema
identity: Each event identifies one opaque Wakterm agent and process incarnation.
Turn-scoped events identify one provider turn without exposing a provider path or parser cursor.
Lifecycle replacement cannot make an old-incarnation event look current.
catalog: A snapshot can enumerate active and recently unavailable agents with display metadata sufficient for conservative Panetone route binding.
Catalog and lifecycle observations have an ordering relationship with the event cursor.
Duplicate display titles remain distinguishable by opaque identity and produce an ambiguity at the Panetone locator boundary.
submission: Prompt acceptance returns a durable request and agent-incarnation receipt.
Possible acceptance without a receipt is explicitly indeterminate and is never represented as safe to retry.
Unsupported capability, unavailable agent, stale incarnation, busy agent, invalid request, and internal observer failure are classified separately.
events: Assistant text preserves provider-observed order and Unicode content.
Plans are distinguishable from ordinary assistant text while retaining a user-visible projection.
Turn start, transition, final, observer failure, and lifecycle change are distinguishable event kinds.
A final is bound to its exact agent incarnation and provider turn.
The existing return-request terminal event remains available while the general stream is additive.
cursor: Every durable event has a strictly increasing sequence.
Reading after sequence N returns only later events in the same durable order.
Restart preserves committed events and sequence monotonicity.
A cursor older than retained history returns an explicit cursor_too_old error with recovery metadata instead of silently starting at the tail.
Retention cannot remove an event still needed by an advertised durable consumer cursor without surfacing the gap.
compatibility: Capabilities and schema versions are negotiated before event consumption.
Unknown semantic event kinds or incompatible major versions fail explicitly.
Golden request, receipt, catalog, event, cursor-gap, and classified-error fixtures are owned by Wakterm and consumed cross-repository.
shadow: Panetone can resume from a saved sequence without producing outbound side effects.
A recording sink can compare ordered Codex user-visible projections with the legacy reader.
Every difference is classified as equivalent formatting, explained intended change, provider-reader defect, Agent API defect, or indeterminate correlation.
Discovery output is not production promotion evidence.
